provenance.primary: OODA Loop (Boyd) — Orient phase: update mental model from observations
provenance.tertiary: Deming PDCA — Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle applied to harness improvement

embeddingInHarness.currentState: Decision #36 proposed. Artifact harvesting rule exists (.claude/rules/artifact-harvesting.md). /harvest skill exists (project-level). Session archive hook exists. All are pieces of the framework but not connected by a governing rule.
embeddingInHarness.proposedState: Operational learning rule connects: (1) artifact harvesting (what to keep), (2) session archiving (full transcript preservation), (3) AAR production (structured learning), (4) running estimate (carry-forward state), (5) Lagebeurteilung (situation assessment at transitions). embeddingInHarness.keyInsight: This session proved the cycle works: M1-M9 AARs observed problems, surfaced proposals, this reconciliation phase proposes harness changes, and the commander decides which to embed. The cycle is: OBSERVE (agent during mission) -> SURFACE (AAR) -> CONSOLIDATE (S3 reconciliation) -> PROPOSE (amendment to planning brief) -> DECIDE (commander approval) -> EMBED (code/rule/hook change) -> VERIFY (next session observes if fix works).

frameworkProposals.name: Context Rot Mitigation Framework
frameworkProposals.status: Demonstrated in this session, not yet proposed for formal adoption

provenance.primary: Situation Awareness theory (Endsley 1995) — SA degradation in dynamic environments
provenance.secondary: Lagebeurteilung (Bundeswehr) — periodic reassessment prevents blind spots
provenance.tertiary: Periodic Inspection (industrial safety) — scheduled checks prevent failure accumulation

whatItWouldLookLike.rule: NOT a separate rule — embed context rot mitigation into the Mission Command rule (.claude/rules/delegation.md). Context rot is a delegation concern (subagents launched with stale parent context) and a session management concern (long sessions degrade rule salience).

techniques.name: Fresh subagent pattern
techniques.description: Launch short-lived subagents for tasks requiring high rule salience. Fresh context at launch = full salience. Many small agents > few large ones.
techniques.trigger: Session >2 hours old, or >50 tool calls since last delegation

techniques.name: Write-verify-amend cycle
techniques.description: Natural refresh point: S3 writes, Verifier reads fresh, S3 re-reads verifier output. Each step resets salience for the relevant rules.
techniques.trigger: Any S3 output that will be committed or consumed downstream

techniques.name: FRAGORD kill-and-replace
techniques.description: If findings changed since a subagent was launched, kill it and relaunch with updated context rather than trying to patch a stale agent.
techniques.trigger: New findings that contradict a running subagent's premises

techniques.name: Running estimate freshness check
techniques.description: Before producing final output, re-read the running estimate and check for discrepancies with earlier analysis. Surface contradictions rather than silently resolving them.
techniques.trigger: Before any final deliverable (AAR, handoff, dashboard, running estimate update)

techniques.name: Operational learning duty injection
techniques.description: Inject the OBSERVE-SURFACE-PROPOSE-CONNECT duty at the END of delegation prompts (after files are loaded, closest to where agent works — recency bias works in our favor).

embeddingInHarness.currentState: Context rot is mentioned in commander's execution plan for this session but not governed. The delegation duty has 9 components — none address context rot explicitly. The /handoff skill has Lagebeurteilung (periodic reassessment) but it covers session transitions, not within-session degradation.
embeddingInHarness.proposedState: Add context rot mitigation techniques to the Mission Command reference file (reference/framework-mission-command.md). Add a brief mention in the delegation rule. The techniques are not a separate framework — they are tactics within Mission Command that address a known failure mode of long-running agent sessions.
embeddingInHarness.keyInsight: Context rot is not a GOVERNANCE problem (no rule is missing) — it is a PHYSICS problem (LLM context window has recency bias, long sessions dilute rule salience). The mitigation is structural (how you compose agents) not behavioral (telling agents to pay attention). Decision #35 (hooks > coaching for recurring patterns) applies: structural mitigation > behavioral reminders.

frameworkProposals.planningBriefAmendment: Amend decision #3 (Mission Command framework): add context rot mitigation as a subsection of the framework reference. Not a separate decision — it is a tactical concern within Mission Command.
frameworkProposals.leverage: HIGH — addresses the primary failure mode of multi-session, multi-agent operations

frameworkProposals.name: Multi-Agent Orchestration Patterns (codification)
frameworkProposals.status: Demonstrated in 40-agent session, root-caused in M9 AAR, proposed for codification

provenance.primary: Mission Command (Auftragstaktik) — commander's intent enables subordinate initiative, but within governed patterns
provenance.secondary: Choreography vs Orchestration (distributed systems) — the S3 is the orchestrator, patterns define the choreography
provenance.tertiary: Design Patterns (Gang of Four) — named, reusable compositions that communicate intent

patterns.name: WRITE-VERIFY-AMEND
patterns.trigger: S3 output that will be committed or consumed downstream
patterns.composition: S3 writes -> Verifier checks against criteria -> S3 amends based on verification
patterns.example: 40-agent session agents #26-28: S3 writes handoff, Verifier checks 9 criteria, S3 applies 7 amendments
patterns.antiPattern: This session M3 (handoff JSON): S3 wrote, no verifier launched, errors discovered only when commander read it

patterns.name: PARALLEL-INVESTIGATE
patterns.composition: Launch N parallel S2 agents with different framings -> compare results -> select best or synthesize
patterns.example: 40-agent session agents #14-16: 3 carry-forward barrier analyses (A, B, C) compared
patterns.antiPattern: Single S2 with one framing — misses alternative perspectives

patterns.name: S2-CHAIN
patterns.trigger: S2 output reveals a deeper question not in the original mission
patterns.composition: S2 investigates -> results reveal deeper question -> launch follow-up S2 with prior output as input
patterns.example: 40-agent session agents #37-38: S2 scratch deletion RCA -> S2 verification lifecycle gap audit
patterns.antiPattern: Expanding original S2 scope mid-mission — violates single-responsibility

patterns.name: S2-THEN-S3
patterns.composition: S2 investigates -> delegating agent reads and decides -> S3 acts on the decision
patterns.example: 40-agent session agents #5->8: S2 investigates post-push bugs -> S3 updates briefing with AAR findings
patterns.antiPattern: S3 acting without S2 intelligence — produces decisions based on assumptions

patterns.name: WRITE_BLOCKED-RELAUNCH
patterns.composition: Agent produces WRITE_BLOCKED as first output line -> delegating agent retries in foreground
patterns.example: 40-agent session agent #21 blocked -> relaunched as #25 with WRITE_BLOCKED signal
patterns.antiPattern: Assuming background Write will succeed — 3/40 agents were blocked in 40-agent session

embeddingInHarness.currentState: Decision #51 governs write-review loop for plan writing only. Decision #4 governs delegation duty (9 components). Neither addresses multi-agent composition.
embeddingInHarness.proposedState: (1) New reference file: reference/orchestration-patterns.md — documents all 5 patterns with triggers, composition, examples, and anti-patterns. (2) Amend delegation duty: add component 10 (PATTERN-CHECK — before launching, ask 'single agent or multi-agent pattern?'). (3) Extend /handoff skill: add orchestration briefing section. (4) Extend dashboard schema: add workflow chain metadata for connected agent groups.
embeddingInHarness.keyInsight: The 40-agent session's S3 invented these patterns through iterative learning with the commander. They represent emergent solutions to real orchestration problems. Codifying them means future S3 agents start with the vocabulary and triggers, not a blank slate.

frameworkProposals.planningBriefAmendment: Add new decision or amend decision #3: codify 5 orchestration patterns as part of Mission Command framework. Amend decision #4: add component 10 (PATTERN-CHECK). Note that the 40-agent session demonstrated the patterns and this session demonstrated the failure mode when they are not codified.
frameworkProposals.leverage: HIGH — directly addresses M9 root cause

connectionToExistingFrameworks.missionCommand: FP-2 and FP-3 embed INTO Mission Command (decision #3) as subsections of the framework reference. They are not separate frameworks — they are Mission Command concerns.
connectionToExistingFrameworks.operationalLearning: FP-1 IS the formalization of decision #36. It connects existing harness capabilities (harvesting, archiving, AAR, running estimate, Lagebeurteilung) into a governed cycle.
connectionToExistingFrameworks.threeLayerGovernance: All three proposals follow the prevention-detection-audit pattern. FP-1: prevention (rules on what to harvest), detection (hooks that harvest/archive), audit (/audit skill checks completeness). FP-2: prevention (delegation patterns that avoid rot), detection (freshness checks), audit (running estimate discrepancy surfacing). FP-3: prevention (PATTERN-CHECK in delegation duty), detection (proposed hook on Agent tool), audit (dashboard chain metadata).

sessionAsProofOfConcept.whatThisSessionDemonstrated: This session IS the operational learning cycle in action. The S3 observed problems (9 AARs), surfaced proposals (consolidated into this document), and will propose harness changes. The commander decides which to embed. The cycle is self-referential: the mission to formalize operational learning IS an instance of operational learning.
whatWorked: AAR format (decision #44) produced structured, comparable intelligence across 7 investigations
WRITE_BLOCKED signal prevented data loss from 3+ Write denials
Running estimate carried forward key facts and findings within the session
M7 file recovery methodology (CC transcript parsing) worked at 100% recovery rate
whatDidNotWork: Single-agent-per-mission pattern produced investigations without verification
S3 cold-start problem: 9 corrections needed before productive work began
Running estimate in scratch (anti-pattern) because canonical location is gitignored
No orchestration patterns applied despite reading the 40-agent dashboard
Handoff described WHAT was produced but not HOW it was orchestrated
